title: Adaptive Backoff Gateway and Idempotency Token Spec for Multi-Region Failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Multiple services implement ad-hoc retry/timeout/backoff logic with different semantics for idempotency keys and hedged requests. During regional outages we observe cascading retries, uneven latency inflation, and customer-facing errors despite global capacity being available in other regions. This ticket defines an interoperable "Adaptive Backoff Gateway" (ABG) — a thin service/client-layer adapter + SDK contract that standardizes per-request deadlines, SLO-aware backoff curves, hedged-request safeguards, and idempotency token semantics across services and SDKs.
background: Observed incidents in Q4 2025 and early 2026 show repeated multi-region amplification: regional latency spikes cause clients to retry aggressively, circuit breakers trip late, and load shedding triggers inconsistently. Existing docs (ENG-31204, ENG-35671) outline retry principles but lack a concrete adapter and SDK contract for consistent enforcement across runtimes. Product wants predictable latency and fewer false-positive errors for users failing over between regions.
proposal: 1) Define a small, language-agnostic ABG API that maps service SLO budgets to per-request deadlines and to an associated backoff profile. 2) Provide SDK shims (Go/TypeScript/Python/Java) implementing: - idempotency token generation & validation rules, including TTL and canonicalization - default hedging policy with a max fanout and a per-caller budget guard - SLO-aware adaptive backoff curves (initial delay, jitter, growth factor) that are driven by service-configured SLO buckets (p99, p95 targets) - circuit breaker integration points and a standardized shed response type for downstream callers 3) Runtime integration: ABG can be deployed as a sidecar for private deployments or as a middleware in hosted infra; runtime will expose per-model / per-route backoff profiles and token validation endpoints. 4) Observability: metrics and logs for retries, hedged calls, idempotency matches, and shed events with token-level tracing tags.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: - Centralizing backoff logic reduces divergence but introduces an adapter surface that must be highly available; mitigated via multi-region deployment and local SDK fallback. - Hedging improves tail latency but risks resource duplication; we limit hedging by a global per-caller budget and reject hedged fanout when load-shedding is active. - Strong idempotency semantics require storage or deterministic request hashing; we choose a hybrid approach: short-lived in-memory token cache for fast dedupe + an optional durable token store for cross-instance deduplication. - To avoid coupling to a particular SLO definition, ABG accepts numeric SLO hints (ms budgets) and maps them to internal backoff presets.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by Reliability and SDK leads
SDK shims implemented for Go and TypeScript with unit tests
Integration tests demonstrating: (a) only one successful write on duplicate idempotency tokens, (b) no amplification during simulated region outage with ABG-enabled clients
Runtime exposes per-route backoff profiles and emits retry/hedge/shed metrics to Prometheus
Canary rollout plan and runbook drafted and reviewed
Security review completed for idempotency token format and storage
implementation_notes: Phase 1: design + proto SDK (2 sprints). Phase 2: runtime-sidecar + integration tests (3 sprints). Phase 3: SDK rollout to core services + canary (2 sprints). Fallback behavior: if ABG is unreachable, SDK uses a conservative local backoff profile (p95-derived) with no hedging. Token TTL defaults to 5 minutes for in-memory dedupe and configurable up to 24 hours for durable stores.
progress_updates: 2026-02-26 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting with Reliability, Runtime, and SDK leads. Agreed to target runtime-1.22 and to prioritize Go/TS SDKs.
2026-03-03 - Marco Liu: Drafted ABG API proto and initial backoff presets. Uploaded design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RINF/ABG+Design+Doc

2026-03-06 - Leila Gomez (SDK): Implemented token canonicalization and added property-based tests for collision resistance. Branch: github.com/redwood/abg-sdk/tree/feature/token-canon PR: https://github.com/redwood/abg-sdk/pull/17

2026-03-09 - Reliability team: Load-shedding integration spec reviewed. Recommendation: Hedge only for requests with downstream idempotency support; otherwise, hedging disabled. Added as constraint in design doc.

2026-03-12 - Marco Liu: Prototype sidecar that returns per-route backoff profiles. Deployed to staging cluster; preliminary test shows 30% reduction in retry amplification under simulated regional latency spike. PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/842
risks: Adapter outage causing client-level conservative fallback and potential increased latency
Token storage growth if many unique idempotency keys are used without TTL enforcement
Misconfigured SLO-to-backoff mapping could either over-aggressively retry or under-utilize available capacity
testing_plan: Unit tests for SDKs covering token dedupe, canonicalization, and TTL eviction. Integration tests: multi-region chaos test harness that simulates region A degraded, ensures ABG routes to region B with hedging budget respected. Load test verifying hedged requests survive under 2x normal QPS with no extra error signal to callers. Observability tests to ensure metrics emitted: abg_retry_count, abg_hedge_count, abg_idempotency_hits, abg_shed_events.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated SDK support. 2) Canary on non-critical services (search-indexer, internal-batching). 3) Monitor SLOs and retry metrics for 48 hours. 4) Gradual expansion to public-facing routes. Rollback: disable hedging + enable conservative local backoff.
